question: design 11.3 -- does CODEX_HOME / GEMINI_CLI_HOME isolation break auth the way CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR does?
answer: YES for CODEX_HOME, but unlike Claude Code it is fully recoverable by copying auth.json, because Codex stores credentials in a plain file and does NOT use the macOS Keychain.

keychain_evidence.note: codex links Security.framework and vendors the security-framework crate, but the only matching strings are os/macos/keychain*.rs paths from the crate used for TLS root certs. No generic-password item exists for any codex-shaped service name.

token_lifetime.implication: a copied auth.json carries an access token good for at most ~10 days from its issue time; after that the copy must refresh on its own.

cases.setup: CODEX_HOME=<isolated> with auth.json copied in, no config.toml
CODEX_HOME=<isolated>, auth.json is a symlink to another copy
cases.verdict: symlink is followed on READ; write-through on refresh is UNMEASURED

cases.setup: CODEX_HOME=<isolated>, credential supplied only via env
cases.cmd: OPENAI_API_KEY=... / CODEX_AUTH=<auth.json contents> codex login status
cases.stdout: Not logged in / 'agent identity JWT payload is not valid JSON' (CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN)
cases.verdict: NO env-only path. CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN is an agent-identity channel, not the ChatGPT OAuth path.

cases.setup: marion-shaped CODEX_HOME: copied auth.json + config.toml declaring the marion MCP server
cases.cmd: codex mcp list; codex exec --skip-git-repo-check 'Reply with exactly the word: pong'
cases.stdout: pong (3596 tokens); mcp list shows marion enabled with MARION_NODE_TOKEN masked as *****
cases.verdict: END-TO-END OK -- one real model call, isolated CODEX_HOME, real auth
cases.note: an earlier attempt pinned model='gpt-5.1-codex' and got HTTP 400 'not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account'. That is a MODEL error, not an auth error -- the credential was accepted. Do not pin an API-only model in a ChatGPT-auth child.

safety_postcheck.note: no write of any kind to ~/.codex during this spike

marion_implications.verdict: CODEX_HOME isolation is KEEPABLE. Unlike the Claude Code / CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR case, it does not force a fileless launch path.
marion_implications.required_step: the child launcher must seed <agent-dir>/config/auth.json by copying ~/.codex/auth.json (or $CODEX_HOME/auth.json of the parent) before exec'ing the child.
marion_implications.security_cost: this duplicates a live OAuth refresh+access token into every per-node agent dir. N nodes = N copies of a credential that can mint API calls on the user's ChatGPT account. Per-node dirs must be 0700, must be excluded from any archive/upload/artifact path, and should be shredded on node teardown.
marion_implications.note_on_config_toml: config.toml in the isolated CODEX_HOME was parsed correctly and the marion MCP server env token was masked in `codex mcp list` output, so the design's off-ps reason for using config.toml survives isolation intact.

unmeasured: refresh-token rotation: whether a per-node copy that refreshes on its own rotates/invalidates the parent's refresh token. The access token was still valid during the spike so no refresh was triggered. Testing it requires either waiting out the ~10-day access-token lifetime or forcing a refresh, which risks invalidating the user's real session.

symlink write-through: whether Codex's refresh writes through a symlinked auth.json or replaces it via atomic tmp+rename (which would break the link and strand a stale copy). Codex does create a tmp/ dir under CODEX_HOME, which is consistent with rename-based writes, but this was not directly observed.
long-running nodes: whether a node alive past the access-token expiry recovers cleanly by refreshing its own copy.

GEMINI_CLI_HOME: gemini 0.53.0 IS installed and GEMINI_CLI_HOME is a real referenced env var in its bundle. Credentials live at ~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json (0600). A generic-password keychain item for service=gemini DOES exist, so the Gemini answer may differ from the Codex one and CANNOT be assumed. Gemini is not on M1's path, so this half remains unmeasured.
